Information in Healthcare Management

Health information management — data quality, records management and using information for decisions.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe health information management
  • List elements of data quality
  • Explain how information supports management decisions

In simple words

Health information management is the organisation, storage and use of health data and records. Good information management means data is accurate, complete and available when needed.

Managers use information to make decisions about staffing, budgets, quality and services.

Elements of data quality

Element Meaning
Accuracy Data is correct
Completeness All required data is present
Timeliness Data is available when needed
Consistency Data is the same across systems
Relevance Data is useful for the purpose

Uses of health information

  • Staffing and rostering.
  • Budget planning.
  • Quality monitoring and improvement.
  • Reporting to regulators.
  • Service planning.

Nurse’s role

  • Document accurately and completely.
  • Record in real time.
  • Use standard terms and abbreviations.
  • Report data errors.
  • Follow retention and confidentiality rules.

🔴 Good data quality

Good health information is accurate, complete, timely, consistent and relevant. Nurses create this data through careful documentation.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Documentation — accurate, complete, timely records support good decisions.
  • Standard terms — use approved abbreviations and terminology.
  • Data entry — enter data correctly in the electronic record.
  • Reporting — contribute to ward reports and quality data.
  • Confidentiality — protect health information at all times.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Health information management organises, stores and uses health data and records.
  2. Data quality elements: accuracy, completeness, timeliness, consistency, relevance.
  3. Information supports staffing, budgets, quality and service planning.
  4. Nurses create data through accurate, complete documentation.
  5. Use standard terms and abbreviations.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Record in real time or as soon as possible.
  2. Report data errors to supervisors.
  3. Follow retention and confidentiality rules.
  4. Good data supports better management decisions.

📌 Memory trick

Data quality: “A-C-T-C-R” — Accuracy, Completeness, Timeliness, Consistency, Relevance.

60-second revision

  • Health information management = organise, store, use health data.
  • Data quality: accuracy, completeness, timeliness, consistency, relevance.
  • Supports staffing, budgets, quality, services.
  • Nurses create data through documentation.
  • Record in real time; use standard terms; protect confidentiality.

Test yourself

Health information management is:

Answer: B. Health information management organises, stores and uses health data and records.

Data quality element meaning ‘data is correct’:

Answer: B. Accuracy means the data is correct.

Documentation should be recorded:

Answer: B. Document in real time or as soon as possible after care.

Health information supports:

Answer: B. Information supports staffing, budgets, quality monitoring and service planning.

Standard terms and abbreviations are used to:

Answer: B. Standard terms ensure clear communication between all staff.
